Judgment 
1. This appeal is directed against the impugned order dated 03.01.2024, vide which, the relief sought by the respondent (herein) under Section 23 of the Protection of Women from the Domestic Violence Act has been decided by the court of Ms. Renu Chaudhary, the Ld. Metropolitan Magistrate-01 (Mahila Court), North-East District, Karkardooma Courts, Delhi, whereby the appellant (herein) has been directed to pay monthly maintenance to the tune of Rs.6530/- each (Rs.13,000/- in total) CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani to the respondent (herein) and her minor child, from the date of the filing of the petition till they are legally entitled to receive the same or the disposal of the case, whichever is earlier.
2. The brief facts of the case are that the respondent (herein) has filed an application under Section 12/17/18/19/20/22/23 of Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, in the Ld. Trial Court claiming therein that her marriage with the appellant (herein) was solemnized on dated 06.05.2019 in accordance with Hindu Rites and Customs and her parents had spent considerable amount in the said marriage. One son was born out of this wedlock, who is minor and living under the care and custody of respondent (herein). She has levelled allegations of demand of dowry, mental harassment and verbal cruelty against the appellant (herein) and his other family members. She has also stated that she is living in the house of her parents and looking after her child. She has further stated that Prafulla Sabui vs Pooja Rani on 1 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102095006/
1 the appellant (herein) was working as Accounts Manager with Tech Chem Solution at the time of his marriage with her and now he is working with Vaalve Sanitation LLP, apart from it, he is running a tour and travel business. She has also claimed that appellant (herein) is drawing a salary of Rs.24,500/- per month from his job and he is having additional income of Rs.20,000/- per month from his business. She has also claimed Rs.25,000/- per month, as interim maintenance. 
3. The respondents were summoned by the Ld. Trial Court and reply to the said application was filed by the appellant (herein). 
CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani 4. The Ld. Trial Court had opined that since the domestic relationship between the parties to the present lis, has not been challenged. Therefore, the respondent (herein) has become entitled to the relief under the Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act and after hearing the counsels for the parties, the Ld. Trial Court, vide its impugned order, was pleased to grant interim maintenance to the respondent (herein) and her minor child. 
5. Feeling aggrieved by the said order, the appellant (herein) has filed the present appeal. The notice of this appeal was issued to the respondent (herein) and on completion of service, respondent (herein) has appeared along with her Counsel. The record of the Ld. Trial Court is also requisitioned. 
6. I have heard Ld. Counsels for the parties. 
7. Sh. Robin Tyagi, Ld. Counsel for the appellant (herein) has submitted that the monthly salary of this appellant (herein) was Rs.17,671/-, but, sometimes, in view of doing some extra work, he was getting some incentives, so, sometimes, he got Rs.18,500/- or Rs.19,582/- and submitted that the Ld. Trial Court at the time of passing the impugned order under appeal had failed to appreciate that this appellant (herein) had also taken a personal loan for purchasing car and he is paying Rs.9,000/-
per month, as installment thereof and also submitted that the appointment letter placed on the record reveals that per annum income of this appellant (herein) is Rs.2,52,000/- and further submitted that this appellant (herein) is not having any other source of income, CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani except his salary and submitted that since, this appellant (herein) has also taken premises on rent and copy of rent agreement placed on record also reveals that this appellant (herein) is also paying Rs.2200/- per month, as, rent and the Ld. Trial Court was required to consider such deductions of rent and personal loan of car taken by this appellant (herein). He has further submitted that the Ld. Trial Court has failed to appreciate that this appellant (herein) also owns liabilities to pay the rent and installments of the personal car loan and this appellant (herein)
never got monthly salary more than Rs.19,582/- and prayed for setting aside the impugned order under appeal. 
8. On the other hand, Sh. Rajesh Kumar, Ld. Counsel for the respondent (herein) has submitted that this appellant (herein) has admitted in his affidavit filed in the Ld. Trial Court that he is having monthly income of Rs.18,500/- and submitted that this appellant (herein) is also having tour and travel business and visiting card of this appellant (herein) is also placed on the record of the Ld.

2 Trial Court. He has further submitted that this appellant (herein) is having additional income from the said business and this appellant (herein) has not denied the said visiting card of Radhey Radhey Tour & Travels, wherein, name, address and phone number of this appellant (herein) are also mentioned and the Ld. Trial Court had also considered the same visiting card of "Radhey Radhey Tour & Travels". He has also submitted that since the statement of account of this appellant (herein)
placed on the record reveals that this appellant (herein) had received salary of Rs.30,000/- in the month of January 2022 CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani and similar salary in the month of February 2022 and even in the month of March 2022, this appellant (herein) had received Rs.30,000/- salary. He has further submitted that at the time of filing of the affidavit, the Ld. Trial Court started manipulating the record of his salary, as, this appellant (herein) is Accountant by profession and tried to show his income lesser to deprive the respondent (herein) and her minor child from the amount of maintenance, to which, they are entitled and submitted that since, the appellant (herein) has manipulated the record of salary slip, after filing of the case by the respondent (herein) against him and submitted that in the photocopy of the rent agreement dated 25.04.2022, the rent is mentioned, as, Rs.2000/- and in the photocopy of the rent agreement dated 25.07.2022, the rent is mentioned, as, Rs.2200/- and submitted that this appellant (herein) is living in the house of his parents and he has manipulated the rent agreements and submitted that since,
this appellant (herein) did not disclose his actual income from the tour and travel business, so, the Ld. Trial Court has considered the admitted monthly salary of Rs.18,500/- of this appellant (herein)
and assessed his total monthly income, as Rs.20,000/- so, the Ld. Trial Court has rightly granted Rs.6500/- each as maintenance to the respondent (herein) and her minor child and also submitted that if this appellant (herein) had taken any personal car loan and he would have enjoyed the same,
so, same personal loan or alleged rent of Rs.2000/- per month cannot be considered and submitted that there is no illegality or perversity in the impugned order under appeal, so, the same is liable to be upheld and the appeal filed by the appellant (herein) is liable to CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs.
Pooja Rani be dismissed. 
9. I have given thoughtful considerations to the submissions made by the respondent (herein) and the Ld. Counsels for the parties and also perused the record. 
10. The perusal of the record reveals that the respondent (herein) had filed the application u/s 12 read with Sections 17, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22 and 23 of the Protection of Women from the Domestic Violence Act and claimed that she her marriage with the appellant (herein) was solemnized on dated 06.05.2019 as per Hindu Rites and Customs and one male child is born out of this wedlock, who is minor and living under the care and custody of respondent (herein). She has levelled allegations of demand of dowry, mental harassment and verbal cruelty against the appellant (herein) and his other family members. She has also stated that she is living in the house of her parents and looking after her child. She has further stated that the appellant (herein) was working as Accounts Manager with Tech Chem Solution at the time of his marriage with her and now he is working with Vaalve Sanitation LLP, apart from it, he is running a tour and travel business. She has also claimed that appellant (herein) is drawing a salary of Rs.24,500/- per month from his job and he is having additional income of Rs.20,000/- per month from his business. She has also claimed Rs.25,000/-
per month, as interim maintenance claiming therein that she is housewife.

3 11. The appellant (herein) had filed the reply and affidavit in the Ld. Trial Court. The appellant (herein) in his affidavit, filed in CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani the Ld. Trial Court has claimed that his monthly income is Rs.18,500/- per month. The appellant (herein) had not denied the domestic relationship with the respondent (herein).
12. The Ld. Trial Court, vide its impugned order under appeal was pleased to grant Rs.6,500/- per month each to the respondent (herein) and her minor child, who is living under the care and custody of the respondent (herein). 
13. In the case in hand, the respondent (herein) has claimed that the appellant (herein) is drawing salary of Rs.24,500/- per month from his job, he is having additional income of Rs.20,000/- per month from his tour and travel business, run in the name of Rahdey Radhey Tour & Travels. 
Whereas the appellant (herein) had filed the affidavit in the Ld. Trial Court, wherein, he has mentioned the amount of his salary as Rs.18,500/- per month. 
14. No doubt that the respondent (herein) did not produce any cogent proof regarding the salary of the appellant (herein) as Rs.24,500/- and additional income of Rs.20,000/- from the alleged Tour &
Travel business. The Ld. Counsel for the appellant (herein) has submitted that this appellant (herein) has taken a personal loan for car and he is paying Rs.9,000/- per month as installment thereof and submitted that this appellant (herein) is also living in the rented accommodation and he is paying Rs.2,200/- per month as rent thereof. He has also submitted that this appellant (herein)
does not have any other source of income except his salary and submitted that in view of CA No.
18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani better performance sometimes incentives are also paid by the employer of the appellant (herein). But, the perusal of the record of the Ld. Trial Court reveals that the respondent (herein) had filed a visiting card in the Ld. Trial Court in the name of Radhey Radhey Tour and Travels, wherein the name, mobile phone number and address of this appellant (herein) are also mentioned. The Ld. Counsel for respondent (herein) has submitted that the address mentioned in the said visiting card is of the parents of this appellant (herein) and submitted that this appellant (herein) is residing in the house of his parents, on the address, on the address as mentioned in the visiting card of Radhey Radhey Tour & Travels. 
15. The perusal of the appointment letter of this appellant (herein) reveals that CTC of this appellant (herein) w.e.f. 01.12.2021 is mentioned as Rs.2,52,000/- per annum and perusal of the photocopies of statement of account of this appellant (herein) in the HDFC Bank reveals that this appellant (herein) had received Rs.30,000/- in the month of January, 2022 from his employer Inner Space and similarly, Rs.30,000/- were received by this appellant (herein) from the same employer in the month of February 2022 and similarly in the month of March 2022 also, this appellant (herein) had received Rs.30,000/- from his said employer. The perusal of statement of account of this appellant (herein) also reveals that on dated 06.12.2021, this appellant (herein) had received Rs.2,05,000/- in his account from Ashish Sharma. The Ld. Counsel for appellant (herein) has submitted that this appellant (herein) had purchased the car in partnership CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani with Ashish Sharma and for running the same car as taxi and this appellant (herein) is paying Rs.9,000/- per month as installment of the personal car loan, but, this appellant (herein) has concealed this fact that he had also received Rs.2,05,000/- from Ashish Sharma on dated Prafulla Sabui vs Pooja Rani on 1 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102095006/
4 06.12.2021. Since, he has failed to disclose about the said fact of receiving of Rs.2,05,000/- from Ashish Sharma on the said date entry, whereof is reflected in the statement of account of this appellant (herein). Thus, such conduct of this appellant (herein) shows that in order to deprive the respondent (herein) and her minor child from maintenance, who is living under care and custody,
this appellant (herein) has claimed that he is paying Rs.9,000/- per month as installment of the said personal car loan and sought deductions thereof. The appellant (herein) has admitted in his affidavit, filed in the Ld. Trial Court that he is having a salary of Rs.18,500/- per month, but, he failed to disclose his actual income from the tour and travels business. The Ld. Counsel for the appellant (herein) argued in this court that monthly income of the appellant (herein) is Rs.17,671,
but, in view of doing some extra work, he was getting some incentives, so, sometimes he got Rs.18,500/- per month and thus, Ld. Counsel for the appellant (herein) has made the submissions in this court, even which are inconsistent to the contents of the affidavit, filed by the appellant (herein) in the Ld. Trial Court regarding his salary. The perusal of the statement of account of this appellant (herein) shows that this appellant (herein) had also received Rs.30,000/- per month in the month of January 2022, February 2022 and March 2022. 
CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani 16. The Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Kulbhushan Kumar vs. Raj Kumari and Others, (1970) 3 SCC 129 while adjudicating about the deductions, which can be made from the income of the husband before awarding maintenance, was pleased to observe as under:-
"...19 . It was further argued before us that the High Court went wrong in allowing maintenance at 25% of the income of the appellant as found by the Income-tax Department assessment proceedings under the Income-tax Act. It was contended that not only should a deduction be made of income-tax but also of house rent,
electricity charges, the expenses for maintaining a car and the contribution out of salary to the provident fund of the appellant. In our view some of these deductions are not allowable for the purpose of assessment of "free income" as envisaged by the Judicial Committee. Income-tax would certainly be deductible and so would contributions to the provident fund which have to be made compulsorily. No deduction is permissible for payment of house rent or electricity charges. The expenses for maintaining the car for the purpose of appellant's practice as a physician would be deductible only so far as allowed by the income-tax authorities i.e. in case the authorities found that it was necessary for the appellant to maintain a car..." 
17. Similarly, their Lordship of High Court of Delh in case of Nitin Sharma and Others vs. Sunita Sharma & Others (2021 III AD (Delhi) 210) was pleased to hold as under:
"...24. In the opinion of this Court, while calculating the quantum of maintenance,
the income has to be ascertained keeping in mind that the deductions only towards income tax and compulsory contributions like GPF, EPF etc. are permitted and no deductions towards house rent, electric charges, repayment of loan, LIC payments etc. are permitted." 
Prafulla Sabui vs Pooja Rani on 1 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102095006/
5 18. Thus from the law laid down in the abovesaid judgments, it is crystal clear that the alleged amount of Rs.2,200/- regarding alleged rent and Rs.9,000/- regarding the alleged installment of personal car loan cannot be considered for ascertaining the CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani amount of maintenance. 
19. In case, Bhagwan Dutt v. Kamla Devi (1975) 2 SCC 386, the Hon'ble Apex Court had observed the object of Section 125 Cr.P.C. that:
"...19. The object of these provisions being to prevent vagrancy and destitution, the Magistrate has to find out as to what is required by the wife to maintain a standard of living which is neither luxurious nor penurious, but is modestly consistent with the status of the family. The needs and requirements of the wife for such moderate living can be fairly determined, only if her separate income, also, is taken into account together with the earnings of the husband and his commitments..."
20. The Hon'ble Apex Court in case of Chaturbhuj vs. Sita Bai 2008 CriLJ 727 was pleased to hold as under:
"...The object of the maintenance proceedings is not to punish a person for his past neglect, but to prevent vagrancy by compelling those who can provide support to those who are unable to support themselves and who have a moral claim to support. 
The phrase "unable to maintain herself" in the instant case would mean that means available to the deserted wife while she was living with her husband and would not take within itself the efforts made by the wife after desertion to survive somehow."
21. Since the respondent (herein) has claimed that this appellant (herein) is drawing a salary of Rs.24,500/- per month from his job and he is having additional income of Rs.20,000/- per month from his business, but, she did not file any documentary proof in support thereof. Since the appellant (herein) has claimed in his affidavit (filed in the Ld. Trial Court) that he is earning Rs.18,500/- per month. So, taking into consideration the facts and circumstances as discussed herein above, it was permissible for the Ld. Trial Court to indulge in the CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani guess work to assess the monthly income of the appellant (herein) and in the case in hand, the Ld. Trial Court has considered the monthly income of the appellant (herein) on the basis of the affidavit, education, as well as, the visiting card, statement of accounts of this appellant (herein) and assessed the monthly income of this appellant (herein) as Rs.20,000/- per month.
22. So, in the absence of any cogent proof of income of the appellant (herein) from the tour and travels business, the Ld. Trial Court has committed no error, while assessed the monthly income of appellant (herein) as Rs.20,000/- per month. 
23. It is settled principle of law that the law makes provision to strike the balance between the standard of living, status and luxuries that were enjoyed by a spouse in the matrimonial home and after separation. It has been held by the Apex Court that the needs of the parties, capacity to pay etc.
must be taken into account while deciding quantum of maintenance. 
Prafulla Sabui vs Pooja Rani on 1 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102095006/
6 24. In the case of Jasbir Kaur Sehgal (Smt.) v. District Judge, Dehradun & Others, reported at (1997)
7 Supreme Court Cases 7, it has been held as under:
"8. The wife has no fixed abode of residence. She says she is living in a Gurudwara with her eldest daughter for safety. On the other hand the husband has sufficient income and a house to himself. The Wife has not claimed any litigation expenses in this appeal. She is aggrieved only because of the paltry amount of maintenance fixed by the courts. No set formula can be laid for fixing the amount of maintenance. It has,
in the very nature of things, to depend on the facts and circumstance of each case. 
Some scope for liverage can, however, be always there. Court CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani has to consider the status of the parties, their respective needs,
capacity of the husband to pay having regard to his reasonable expenses for his own maintenance and of those he is obliged under the law and statutory but involuntary payments or deductions. The amount of maintenance fixed for the wife should be such as she can live in reasonable comfort considering her status and the mode of life she was used to when she lived with her husband and also that she does not feel handicapped in the prosecution of her case. At the same time, the amount so fixed cannot be excessive or extortionate. In the circumstances of the present case we fix maintenance pendente lite at the rate of Rs.5,000/- per month payable by respondent-husband to the appellant-wife." 
25. Their lordship of Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in the case of Bharat Hegde v. Saroj Hegde, (140 (2007) DLT 16, had culled out following 11 factors, which can be taken into consideration for deciding the application under Section 24 of Hindu Marriage Act, relevant portion of which reads as under:
"8. Unfortunately, in India, parties do not truthfully reveal their income. For self employed persons or persons employed in the unorganized sector, truthful income never surfaces. Tax avoidance is the norm. Tax compliance is the exception in this country. Therefore, in determining the interim maintenance, there cannot be mathematical exactitude. The court has to take a general view. From the various judicial precedents, the under noted 11 factors can be culled out, which are to be taken into consideration while deciding an application under Section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act. The same are:
 (1) Status of the parties.
 (2) Reasonable wants of the claimant. 
 (3) The independent income and property of the claimant. 
 (4) The number of persons, the non applicant has to maintain. 
 (5) The amount should aid the applicant to live in a similar life style as he/she enjoyed in the matrimonial home. 
 (6) Non-applicant's liabilities, if any. 
 (7) Provisions for food, clothing, shelter, education, medical Prafulla Sabui vs Pooja Rani on 1 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102095006/
7 attendance and treatment etc. of the applicant.
 (8) Payment capacity of the non-applicant.
 (9) Some guess work is not ruled out while estimating the income of the non-applicant when all the sources or correct CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani sources are not disclosed. 
(10) The non-applicant to defray the cost of litigation. (11) The amount awarded under Section 125, Cr.P.C. is adjustable against the amount awarded under Section 24 of the Act. 
23. The Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Jasbir Kaur (Smt.) (supra), has also recognized the fact that spouses in the proceedings for maintenance do not truthfully disclose their true income and therefore some guess work on the part of the Court is permissible. Further the Hon'ble Supreme Court has also observed that "considering the diverse claims made by the parties one inflating the income and the other suppressing an element of conjecture and guess work does enter for arriving at the income of the husband. It cannot be done by any mathematical precision". 
26. The Hon'ble Apex Court in Neeta Rakesh Jain v. Rakesh Jeetmal Jain reported at AIR 2010 SC 3540, has laid guidelines which the courts may keep in mind at the time of fixing the quantum of maintenance. 
"In other words, in the matter of making an order for interim maintenance, the discretion of the court must be guided by the criterion provided in the Section,
namely, the means of the parties and also after taking into account incidental and other relevant factors like social status; the background from which both the parties come from and the economical dependence of the petitioner. Since an order for interim maintenance by its very nature is temporary, a detailed and elaborate exercise by the court may not be necessary, but, at the same time, the court has got to take all the relevant factors into account and arrive at a proper amount having regard to the factors which are mentioned in the statute". 
27. Coming to the case in hand, since the appellant (herein) had admitted his monthly income as Rs.18,500/- in the Ld. Trial Court, but, he failed to clarify about his business of tour and travels, run in the name of Radhey Radhey Tour and Travels and additional income therefrom. So, as per the law discussed herein above, it was permissible for the Ld. Trial Court to indulge in the guess work and the Ld. Trial Court after indulging in the guess CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani work and after considering the abovesaid facts, has correctly assessed the monthly income of the appellant (herein) as Rs.20,000/-.
28. Since their lordship of High Court of Delhi in case Annurita Vohra vs. Sandeep Vohra 2004 (74)
DRJ 99 had laid down the guidelines regarding the quantum of maintenance, so, taking into consideration the fact that the respondent (herein) is having one minor child, who is also living under care and custody of respondent (herein), the Ld. Trial Court was required to grant Rs.5,000/-
Prafulla Sabui vs Pooja Rani on 1 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/102095006/
8 per month each to the respondent (herein) and her minor child, but, the Ld. Trial Court after assessing the monthly income of the appellant (herein) as Rs.20,000/- per month, has granted Rs.6,500/- each to the respondent (herein) and her minor child. So, such error committed by the Ld. Trial Court, while deciding the share of the respondent (herein) and her minor child needs to be rectified. So, the same error is rectified by this and the amount of interim maintenance granted by the Ld. Trial Courts to the respondent (herein) and her minor child as Rs.6500/- each (total amount of Rs.13,000/-) is reduced to Rs.5,000/- each to the respondent (herein) and her minor child (total amount of Rs.10,000/-) and thus, the amount of maintenance awarded by the Ld. Trial Court is modified in the light of the law laid down by the Hon'ble High Court of Delhi in case "Annurita Vohra vs. Sandeep Vohra, 2004 (74) DRJ 99". The appellant (herein) is directed to pay Rs.5,000/-
per month each to the respondent (herein) and her minor child (total amount of Rs.10,000/-) from the date of filing of application in the Ld. CA No. 18/2024 Praful Sabui Vs. Pooja Rani Trial Court till they are legally entitled or till the disposal of the case in the Ld. Trial Court. 
29. It is clarified that nothing express hereinabove shall affect the merit of the case. 
30. In the abovesaid terms, the appeal filed by the appellant (herein) stands disposed of. 
31. The file be consigned to record room. The record of the Ld. Trial Court is ordered to be returned with the attested copy of this judgment.
